title: What to Watch This Week: Dragons Return, Carmy Says Goodbye, and a Jungle Reopens
excerpt: House of the Dragon brings the fire, The Bear plates its final service, and Welcome to the Jungle storms theatres. Our opinionated guide to the seven titles worth your weekend — and exactly where the diaspora can stream them.
body:
Some weeks the streaming calendar dribbles out filler. This is not one of those weeks. Between June 22 and June 28, the platforms are dropping the return of TV's most expensive soap opera, the farewell season of its most stressful kitchen drama, and a jungle full of Bollywood's loudest comedians — all at once. Here's where to point the remote, and where the diaspora can actually find each one.

House of the Dragon, Season 3 — the one you clear the calendar for

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xZUavocHU2g

The Dance of the Dragons is no longer simmering. It's a full boil. Season 3 picks up with Queen Rhaenyra (Emma D'Arcy) and the rest of House Targaryen tipping from cold war into open slaughter, and the casting additions — James Norton, Dan Fogler, Tommy Flanagan as the Lord of Winterfell — signal that the battlefield is about to get crowded. After two seasons of people glowering across candlelit tables, this is the season the dragons actually go to work. Where to watch: HBO Max in the US, Sky/NOW in the UK, Crave in Canada, and JioHotstar for the desi crowd back home and abroad. This is appointment viewing. Block out Sunday night.

The Bear, Final Season — the goodbye nobody's ready for

**"https://x.com/Tyre_94/status/2068738285728321605

The Bear, Final Season — the goodbye nobody's ready for

It's the last service for Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto."**

It's the last service for Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto. Jeremy Allen White's Emmy magnet returns Thursday for its closing chapter, with Carmy threatening to walk and Sydney (Ayo Edebiri), Richie (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) and the rest left to fight for that Michelin star before the lights go out for good. If you've ever worked a kitchen, a startup, or any room where everyone's yelling because they care too much, this show has had your number for years. Where to watch: Hulu in the US (all episodes at once), Disney+ internationally, JioHotstar in India. Bring tissues and a snack — you'll need both.

Avatar: The Last Airbender, Season 2 — Netflix's redemption arc continues

!Dan Fogler — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The live-action adaptation that surprised the doubters is back Thursday. Season two sends Aang, Katara and Sokka into the Earth Kingdom to master earthbending, and with the show already wrapped through its planned three-season run, there's a confidence here the first outing lacked. Where to watch: Netflix, everywhere. The most family-friendly pick on this list, and a genuinely good one for diaspora households juggling kids and a nostalgia itch.

Blast — the Tamil sleeper hits streaming

A mining-scam thriller wrapped around a martial-arts family drama, Blast marks the directorial debut of Subash K. Raj and rode a surprisingly lucrative theatrical run before landing on streaming. Arjun anchors it alongside Preity Mukhundhan and Abhirami. Where to watch: Netflix from June 25, in the original Tamil with Telugu, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam dubs — so no matter which South Indian language your family argues in, there's a version for you.

Ananthan Kaadu — for the theatre purists

If you'd rather smell the popcorn, Arya's Malayalam-Tamil political action thriller lands in theatres June 25. Set across the politically charged 1980s and '90s, it follows a young man rising against exploitation to protect his land and his people — gritty, period, and unafraid. Where to watch: In cinemas, including select overseas screens that carry Malayalam and Tamil releases.

Welcome to the Jungle — the loudest ticket of the week

Love it or roll your eyes at it, Welcome 3 is the event release of the week, hitting theatres June 26 after eighteen years and forty-odd stars. Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Disha Patani and Jacqueline Fernandez headline a comedy that survived fourteen CBFC cuts on its way to Friday. Is it high art? Absolutely not. Is it the kind of big, dumb, ensemble masala that fills a Friday-night hall in Edison and Southall with the whole family? Completely. Where to watch: In cinemas worldwide — this one's built for the big screen and the overseas weekend.

Drishyam 3 — if you somehow missed it

Still catching up? Mohanlal's Georgekutty returned last week on Prime Video, and the diaspora finally has access to the twist everyone's been whispering about. Where to watch: Amazon Prime Video, in Malayalam with Telugu, Tamil and Kannada versions. Four-and-a-half years on from the last chapter, and still the smartest cat-and-mouse game in Indian cinema.

My pick of the week? If you only have time for one, make it The Bear's finale — TV doesn't say goodbye to something this good very often. But if you want the spectacle, the dragons are right there, breathing fire. Either way, the couch is the place to be this weekend.
